new_entities.name: At-home red light panel
new_entities.description: Consumer red or near-infrared light panels marketed for home use to improve skin tone, wrinkles, or skin recovery.

new_entities.name: Skin outcomes
new_entities.description: Visible or measured skin-related outcomes such as wrinkles, erythema, healing, or rejuvenation.

edges.effect_quant: A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis of light-emitting diode skin studies found the most consistent pooled improvements in psoriasis and skin rejuvenation subsets, while a 2008 facial-photoaging trial reported visible improvement in fine lines and wrinkles in 74% of 22 treated participants after handheld red and near-infrared LED use.
edges.population: adults using home or clinic-style red and near-infrared LED photobiomodulation devices for aesthetic skin concerns
edges.mechanism: Red and near-infrared light may alter mitochondrial signaling, wound-healing pathways, and collagen-related processes, but outcomes depend heavily on wavelength, dose, device design, and treatment target.
edges.summary: At-home red-light devices have a plausible and moderately supportive skin literature, but the evidence is not uniform across indications or device types. The most defensible claim is modest benefit for selected skin endpoints rather than a universal rejuvenation effect.
edges.caveats: Do not generalize positive clinic-style LED studies to every consumer light panel. Evidence for efficacy varies by protocol, and long-term cosmetic benefit is less certain than short-term improvement in selected measures.

evidence.citation: Khalid M et al 2022 Photodermatol Photoimmunol Photomed
evidence.notes: Utilization of light-emitting diodes for skin therapy: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
